messages:
maria.support: FYI — customer emily-customer opened a ticket: their alert 'errors / requests > 1%' has been firing every 5m since ~03:00 UTC despite low traffic. attaching screenshot.
emily-customer: we saw 20+ alerts last night. traffic at our end was steady (dev traffic), nothing that should trigger this. happy to share logs.
maria.support: steps from customer: 1) 02:55 deploy that touched client SDK 2) low qps 3) alerts start firing ~03:00 and spike every 5m. they included a CSV of events.
kevin-oncall: thanks — can you paste the metric query and the alert thresholds? also need the raw series for errors and requests for 02:50-03:10 UTC.
maria.support: alert rule: WHEN sum(errors, 5m) / sum(requests, 5m) > 0.01 FOR 1m
query snippets from infra:
```
# errors series
sum by (service)(increase(api.errors_total[5m]))
# requests series
sum by (service)(increase(api.requests_total[5m]))
```
kevin-oncall: interesting — both use 5m increase(), but are these using the same timestamp alignment? we had a recent change that defaulted to ingestion_timestamp for counters; requests still use event_timestamp in the pipeline.
liam-analytics: confirming: pipeline A (ingest path) now stamps metrics with ingestion_ts when we do delta/derive; our rollup job uses bucket origin = epoch for requests but origin = ingestion_time for errors because of order of transforms. result: counts can be attributed to adjacent buckets when there is ~90-120s ingestion lag.
kevin-oncall: that mismatch will cause intermittent windows where requests are 0 but errors show up (or vice versa), producing a huge ratio. sounds like a classic alignment bug.
maria.support: repro steps provided by emily: replay CSV through our ingestion with simulated 80s delay and run both rollups; they reproduced alert spikes.
emily-customer: can you explain why it started after our 02:55 deploy? we didn't change anything server side.\nliam-analytics: the deploy triggered a client-side batching change causing many events to be delivered in short bursts (timing shift). combined with ingestion lag, the misaligned buckets overlapped differently after that traffic pattern changed.
kevin-oncall: short-term mitigation: update alert to use a longer evaluation window or add a smoothing rule. but root fix is to align aggregation window origins and use consistent timestamp field.
kevin-oncall: quick hotfix I pushed to prod aggregator config: set rollup.bucket_origin = event_timestamp for both errors and requests. restarted rollup at 03:40 UTC. monitoring now.
sre-bot: deploy: rollup-config-update to prod by kevin-oncall at 1769572800 — status: success
maria.support: customer notified about mitigation and that we're investigating root cause. emily, do you want alerts silenced while we validate? :slightly_smiling_face:
emily-customer: yes please, silenced for the next 2 hours would be great.
kevin-oncall: validating metrics post-fix — initial check shows alerts stopped firing. raw time-series now line up; attached sample plot.
liam-analytics: filed GH issue #2481: "Aggregation timestamp mismatch — rollup origin inconsistent between transforms" with repro instructions, config diff, and suggested test. tagging infra/metrics.
maria.support: leaving note in ticket and offering credit for noisy alerts. will follow up with postmortem.
kevin-oncall: followups: 1) add unit test for origin alignment 2) add e2e replay test with delayed ingestion 3) add alert-runbook explaining alignment pitfall
maria.support: thanks all — will close loop with customer once we confirm stability. :heart:
